title: Feature Hatchery — lightweight composer for micro-features
content:
This is a messy scratchpad for an idea I've been noodling on: a 'Feature Hatchery' — a tiny, composable builder experience that lets product managers and PM-adjacent folks prototype small LLM-driven features without a full engineering rollout. Purpose: speed up validated learning for micro-features (snippets, assistants, single-surface automations) and make A/B-able artifacts that can graduate to proper SDK/integration once proven.

Context / motivation:
- Teams currently iterate on LLM features either as quick hacked-in demos (fragile, unobservable) or full projects (slow). We lack a low-friction middle: durable prototypes with basic telemetry, rate-limits, and rollout knobs.
- PMs/UX should be able to assemble small blocks (prompt template + instruction + post-processor) and test with internal traffic, collect quality metrics, then hand-off.

Core idea (first-pass):
- A web UI "hatchery" where a user creates a Feature Card: name, surface (chat/snippet/embed/rewrite), prompt template, sample inputs, simple post-processing (trim, regex redaction, format JSON), and a small eval set.
- Each card gets an API endpoint + embed in Console for a short-lived trial (configurable TTL, throttles).
- Built-in telemetry: per-request latency, token counts, success rate (user-defined pass/fail on eval set), and sample outputs snapshot.
- Quick rollout toggles: internal-only, % sample traffic, or route by header.

Goals (what success looks like):
- <4 day experiment lifecycle from idea -> measurable signal (qual/quant).
- 30% fewer engineering hours for first-validation of new micro-features across pilot teams.
- Enough telemetry to decide: kill, iterate, or engineer.

User stories (rough):
- PM: I want to prototype an FAQ rewriter to reduce support answers so I can check coverage on 100 queries in 48h.
- Designer: I want to try a micro-summarizer inserted into the article view and preview outputs on sample pages.
- SRE: I want each hatchery feature to run in bounded resources with clear quotas.

Acceptance / minimum viable surface:
- UI to create/edit Feature Card (name + surface + prompt + sample set).
- One-click spin-up that produces a discoverable endpoint and embed snippet.
- Per-card telemetry dashboard (requests, tokens, avg latency, sample outputs).
- Eval harness: upload 50 examples, run them, and compute pass rate via regex or simple comparator.
- Rollout controls: on/off, % sampling, internal-only flag.

Technical notes / constraints:
- Security: features should default to scrubbed logs and redaction; opt-in for raw output retention. KMS for secrets.
- Resource model: hosted trial runs should be rate-limited to prevent runaway costs. Consider per-card budget (daily token cap).
- Compatibility: integrate with existing routing + fallback policies; when a hatchery feature is down, route to fallback model/variant.

Experiments to run first:
- Pilot with support team rewriter: measure changes in time-to-answer and deflection. (Metric hooks: deflection rate, pass-rate on eval).
- Internal UX prototype for summarizer in Console articles; measure NPS from a small cohort.
- Cost-sim: run 10 hatchery cards for 2 weeks and compute per-feature cost and token pattern.

Open questions / risks:
- Ownership: who vets production-readiness? Need a clear handoff checklist when an experiment graduates.
- RBAC: non-devs creating endpoints is risky — need role gating and approvals.
- Eval fidelity: simple regex won't catch hallucinations. How to add human labeling cheaply?
- Drift/maintenance: will teams leave many stale hatchery endpoints active? Need TTL + expired-state.

Next steps (personal to-do):
- Sketch quick UI flow in Figma and get 30-min sync with Maya + Rohan.
- Wire up a tiny prototype using hosted-api + a lambda shim for post-processing. Aim for internal demo in ~2 weeks.
- Draft the handoff checklist: tests, telemetry thresholds, runbook items, compliance sign-off.

Random ideas to consider later:
- Template marketplace: shareable prompt components and post-processors inside the org.
- One-click promote: convert hatchery card into a proper route in Console with prefilled configs and a migration checklist.
- Built-in canary with quality gates: if pass rate drops below threshold, automatically reduce traffic.

Notes-to-self: keep scope tiny for MVP. Focus on 3 surfaces (snippet, chat injection, rewrite). Make telemetry first-class — teams will make decisions based on it.

-- Ivy
